that he used to consider disliked (makruh) the residue (leftover drinking water) of every creature whose flesh may not be eaten.

key_terms.سُؤْر: Suur - the residue or leftover water from which an animal has drunk; jurisprudential term used in fiqh of taharah
key_terms.لَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: That whose flesh is not eaten - the Sharia category of animals whose consumption is forbidden
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: Yukrahu - to consider makruh (religiously disliked/reprehensible), a technical fiqh term for the grade between permissible and forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is the leftover water of animals whose meat is forbidden considered impure for wudu in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) considered it religiously disliked (makruh) to use for wudu the leftover drinking water of animals whose flesh is forbidden to consume. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle that ritual purity is linked to the permissibility of the animal: carnivores, predatory birds, and animals rendered impure by their nature are among those whose suur (residual water) is considered makruh for use in ablution. The original audience of Shia jurists understood this as a legal opinion that does not render the water najis but places it in a state of religious reprehensibility.
